selection.rationale: Objective ttft_ms is the prefill forward on the frozen 256-token prompt (adapter run(): one model(...) call with logits_to_keep=1, argmax, explicit torch.cuda.synchronize); decode must still run but is not scored. Independently measured baseline ttft_ms=24.12 against 21.46ms diagnostic prefill CUDA time, and the Qwen3DecoderLayer region owns 20.60ms of it, so this region effectively is the metric. Leaf-level composition of the 36 prefill layer executions (diagnostic CUDA, RTX 4090, nested times not summed): projection GEMMs 15.55ms (75%; MLP gate/up+down 11.51ms running ~120-124 TFLOPS, i.e. ~73-75% of the 165 TFLOPS BF16 ceiling, q/kv/o 4.04ms), SDPA only 0.73ms, and ~4.3ms (21%) in unfused elementwise chains: 145 Qwen3RMSNorm instances expanded into to.dtype/pow/mean/add/rsqrt/mul kernels (including q_norm/k_norm), HF rotary application expanded into cat/neg/mul/mul/add per layer, residual adds and SiLU*up muls - roughly 700+ tiny kernels on [1,256,2560] tensors per prefill. lm_head (0.83ms) sits outside the region and is already near the memory roofline (~940GB/s of ~1008GB/s), as are SDPA and the embedding. The same layer-forward code executes 31 more times in the decode phase (observed as 36 site-bucketed calls with 31 invocations each; clean decode is 22.4ms/step and launch-bound), so the coherent editable boundary is the decoder-layer forward implementation shared by both phases: groups bfbb82bf9eea3f763cd0 (prefill) and 2555b869558ffdba52b4 (decode), with affected_calls covering every observed call in both subtrees (3564 prefill + 21888 decode). The edit lands in the project source (module-forward restructuring at model level in qwen_inference.py); no reordering of cross-module dependencies is proposed.
selection.hypothesis: Restructuring the decoder-layer forward reduces ttft_ms: (a) fuse the RMSNorm chain, rotary application, residual add and SiLU*up into single kernels per site (e.g. via torch.compile on the decoder layers or equivalent hand-fused implementations), replacing ~700+ elementwise kernel launches and ~4.3ms of prefill elementwise CUDA time with an estimated ~1-1.5ms; (b) project gate and up through one pre-concatenated [19456,2560] weight (72->36 wide GEMMs per prefill, N=19456 tiles better across 128 SMs), for an estimated further 0.4-0.8ms. Expected ttft_ms ~24.1 -> ~20.5-21.5 (-10-15%) with logits within atol/rtol=0.02 and identical greedy tokens, since BF16 cuBLAS GEMMs with fp32 accumulation (TF32 disabled) and fp32 norm arithmetic keep the same math; decode runs the same code and must still emit the exact 32 tokens. These are hypotheses to be tested by the framework paired measurement, not accepted benefits; diagnostic CUDA durations are navigation evidence only.

proposal.rationale: Selected region: the 36 Qwen3DecoderLayer executions of the prefill phase (group bfbb82bf9eea3f763cd0, ~20.6ms of the 21.46ms diagnostic prefill CUDA time and effectively the ttft_ms metric) plus their 31-invocation decode-phase counterparts (group 2555b869558ffdba52b4), as one coherent decoder-layer forward boundary shared by both phases. inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so this is the first attempt; the deviations from the selection hypothesis sketch are driven by direct CPU replication evidence described below. Gate analysis that shaped the design: the evaluator compares every element of the quality-run logits tensor against the unmodified baseline with atol=rtol=0.02 and requires exactly equal greedy tokens. I replicated the full 36-layer stack on CPU in BF16 with the real asset weights and the real chat-templated 256-token input. Fusing the RMSNorm chains (single-rounding F.rms_norm or torch.compile-style fusion) or merging gate/up (and q/k/v) GEMMs changes results by 1 ulp on a small fraction of elements, and those ulp-level differences amplify through the residual stream to logits differences of up to ~0.5 absolute, breaching the tolerance on 5-13% of vocabulary elements (greedy tokens stayed equal, the all-element logits check would not pass). A dose-response test showed that even ~5 single-ulp flips anywhere in the norm outputs across the stack reproduce that envelope, while an op-for-op identical kernel sequence is bit-exact. The selection hypothesis (a)/(b) elements that change rounding (fused norms, packed GEMMs) therefore had to be dropped; what remains is everything that removes time without changing a single kernel result. Change 1 - lean host path: one pre-bound callable per physical layer replaces the transformers 5.16.1 Python path (GradientCheckpointingLayer/attention/MLP/norm/linear/act sub-module __call__ dispatch, hook checks, kwargs plumbing, attention-interface resolution, ~90 host-side aten invocations per layer). The aten op sequence, shapes, strides, dtypes and values issued are identical to the reference implementation (input/post RMSNorm chains, q/k/v projections, q_norm/k_norm, HF rotary application with rotate_half, DynamicCache.update, the exact sdpa_attention_forward logic including the enable_gqa=True condition, is_causal=q_len>1-and-mask-None, the kv-slice branch, transpose+contiguous, o_proj, residual adds, gate/up/down MLP with SiLU). CPU parity with real weights: bit-exact hidden states after all 36 layers, bit-exact KV cache, bit-exact logits after 3 decode steps, for prefill [1,256,2560] and decode [1,1,2560] signatures. Change 2 - prefill CUDA graphs: for each physical layer, the second invocation with the frozen prefill signature (batch 1, 256 tokens, contiguous BF16, attention_mask None, empty DynamicCache - always inside the framework untimed warmup/reference runs, since >=6 prefill invocations precede the timed repeats: reference generation, reset checks, identity controls, quality checks, warmup 2, repeats 5) captures that eager kernel stream into a per-layer CUDA graph over a single shared capture pool, captured in live-run order 0..35 with each graph reading the previous graph output slot. Steady-state prefill then performs one input copy, one cos/sin copy and 36 graph replays instead of ~2100 kernel launches. Replay executes the identical kernels with identical pointers, so outputs remain bit-exact; the launch-gap portion of ttft (24.12ms wall vs 21.46ms diagnostic CUDA time, plus per-layer host dispatch) is what this removes. Every kernel re-executes on every invocation; nothing about the fixture (inputs, outputs, rotary tables, logits, tokens) is cached - cos/sin and hidden states are copied fresh from the live invocation tensors each run. Why the consumers of eliminated inner calls remain valid: the layer replacement returns the same hidden_states tensor the baseline layer returns, and it performs the same DynamicCache.update bookkeeping (during capture) or rebinds the current cache object layer to the graph-owned key/value tensors (on replay, attribute assignment only). The parent Qwen3Model loop, final norm, lm_head, argmax, and every decode step therefore consume bit-identical values and an equivalently-behaving cache, so all external outputs (tokens, logits, timing structure) are unchanged. Safety: decode-length calls (sequence length 1) and any other signature (different batch/length/dtype/strides, non-None mask, non-DynamicCache, non-empty cache for the layer) never touch graphs and run the bit-exact eager path; the first compatible prefill invocation always runs eager; any capture or replay exception permanently disables graphs for that layer and falls back to the same eager path, so the worst case is the un-accelerated (still bit-exact) behavior of Change 1 alone. No parameters are repacked or re-pointed (the packed-GEMM variant from the hypothesis was rejected by the drift evidence), so warm-model state, aliasing and reset semantics are untouched. Expected effect (hypothesis for the paired measurement, not a claimed benefit): ttft_ms 24.12 -> roughly 21.5-22.3ms (removing most of the ~2.7ms non-CUDA wall gap and inter-kernel launch overhead; GPU kernel stream unchanged). Decode is not scored but also gets the lean host path; its kernels are unchanged.

setup_work.when: Lazy, on the worker: at build() only module references and per-layer callables are created (no GPU work, no allocation). CUDA graph capture happens at each layer second compatible prefill invocation, which falls in the framework untimed warmup/reference phase; nothing setup-related executes inside timed runs.
setup_work.steps: Per layer: 2 eager warmup forwards on a shared side stream with a throwaway DynamicCache, one capture into the shared pool, one immediate replay plus synchronize to produce that invocation real outputs. Total one-time GPU work ~36x4 layer forwards (~120-150ms), CPU-bound capture overhead included, all outside timing.
setup_work.memory: Persistent additions: shared capture pool holding 36 graph output slots (~1.3MB each), 36 layers of graph-owned K/V tensors (~1.05MB each), per-capture transient high-water (~45MB, pool blocks recycled between sequential captures) and shared static cos/sin plus one input slot: on the order of 150-200MB extra reserved and ~90MB extra allocated. The warmup side stream retains its transient blocks (~45MB reserved). cuBLAS workspaces for the capture stream live in the pool. Expect framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes to include this setup; per-run peak_allocated_bytes should be similar to or slightly below baseline because steady-state replay no longer re-allocates the ~45MB per-layer transient chain every run (those allocations moved into the retained capture pool, whose blocks raise reserved instead). No weights are duplicated, repacked or freed, so the 8GB parameter set is unchanged.
setup_work.state_and_sync: Single stream during replay (graphs replay on the current stream in layer order 0..35); the explicit torch.cuda.synchronize at the ttft boundary and the final workload synchronize see identical stream semantics. KV cache tensors returned to the adapter are graph-pool tensors rebound per run before decode; decode steps and the next run prefill replay overwrite them only after the previous run completed (sequential single-stream execution). No collectives, no extra streams at steady state, no host threads.

quality_risks: Bit-exactness is the design invariant: the eager path issues the identical aten op sequence of transformers 5.16.1 and CUDA graph replay re-executes exactly those kernels, so logits and tokens are expected to match the baseline exactly (CPU replication with real weights confirmed bit-exact hidden states, cache and logits for prefill and decode). Residual risk is limited to cross-invocation library nondeterminism (cuBLAS/flash heuristic changes between invocations), which would affect the paired baseline equally.

If graph capture fails in the worker environment (profiler active, capture-unsafe allocation, allocator policy), affected layers permanently fall back to the bit-exact eager path; quality stays correct and only the launch-overhead saving is lost.

The eliminated inner call sites (24372 functional + 1008 module observations in the two groups) no longer execute under their original parents in steady state (their kernels replay inside per-layer CUDA graphs); discovery recapture should re-attribute or drop them accordingly. If the framework reinstated the original parents mid-run, the same eager path would reproduce their behavior op-for-op.
Decode-phase behavior is untouched except for host-side dispatch; its kernels, cache growth and greedy-token path are identical to baseline.
No sampling, batching, sequence-length, generation-count or data semantics are modified; the workload executes in full on every invocation.
